name: Israel-Hezbollah war in Lebanon (2026)
summary: Hezbollah reopened fire on 2 March 2026 after the US-Israeli war on Iran began, and Israel answered with its deepest invasion of Lebanon in a generation, crossing the Litani and taking Beaufort. Since a 19 June ceasefire Israel holds a 570-600 sq km 'security zone' behind its own Yellow Line, while a US-brokered Israel-Lebanon framework asks the Lebanese army to disarm Hezbollah zone by zone.

sides.name: Israel
leaders: Eyal Zamir (Chief of the General Staff)
sides.strength: Five divisions committed at peak in spring 2026 (Al Jazeera via Wikipedia); by Oct 2026 Northern Command was reducing brigade combat teams in a winterised 'forward defense' posture (LWJ, 7 Oct 2026).

sides.name: Hezbollah
backers: Iran (IRGC Quds Force advisers, funding, arms)
sides.strength: No reliable post-war 2026 estimate retrieved. Older pre-2024 estimates: 40,000-120,000 rockets, thousands of ATGMs, 20,000 full-time fighters plus 20,000 reservists (Janes 2017) or about 45,000 (Israeli assessment 2018) (Wikipedia: Hezbollah armed strength); these predate heavy losses in 2024 and 2026. In 2026 it fired up to about 2,000 rockets and drones into Israel and fielded ATGMs and fibre-optic FPV drones (Wikipedia: 2026 Lebanon war).

sides.name: Lebanese state (not a belligerent against Israel)
backers: United States (military aid tied to disarmament milestones)
leaders: Simon Karam (negotiator in talks with Israel)
sides.strength: LAF claimed 'operational control' in three pilot zones by Sep 2026 and listed 1,818 weapons and ammunition items seized (LWJ, Sep 2026).

background: Israel and Hezbollah fought from October 2023 in support of Gaza, escalating in September-November 2024 with the pager attacks, the killing of Hassan Nasrallah and an Israeli ground invasion, ended by a November 2024 ceasefire. Israel kept five hilltop positions and struck Lebanon almost daily, killing 331 people (at least 127 civilians) by November 2025, and assassinated Hezbollah's chief of staff Haytham Ali Tabatabai in Beirut in November 2025.

When the US and Israel struck Iran on 28 February 2026 and killed Ali Khamenei, Hezbollah entered the war on 2 March. Lebanon's government, which had already declared a state monopoly on arms and sent the army south of the Litani, banned Hezbollah's military activities and opened the first direct talks with Israel since 1983. The war matters because it decides whether Hezbollah survives as an armed force and whether southern Lebanon becomes a long-term Israeli-held buffer.
year: From 2 March Israel struck Beirut's southern suburbs (Dahiyeh), the Bekaa and the south, killing intelligence chief Hussain Makled, Quds Force officers at a Beirut hotel (8 March) and dozens in Nabi Chit (7 March). Ground forces entered border towns from 3 March and launched a full ground operation on 16 March; Defense Minister Katz announced demolition of border villages and control up to the Litani on 24 March. Five divisions fought for Khiam and Bint Jbeil, which the 98th Division encircled by 13 April. On 8 April, hours after the US-Iran ceasefire, 'Operation Eternal Darkness' hit more than 100 targets in ten minutes, killing at least 357.

A US truce took effect on 16-17 April, but Israel kept its positions and declared a Yellow Line around 55 villages. Fighting continued under the truce: the IDF crossed the Litani in early May, was repelled at Haddatha (19-21 May) and captured Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, Yohmor and Beaufort Castle (27-31 May), then ordered evacuation of everything south of the Zahrani. Hezbollah introduced fibre-optic FPV drones and killed four 401st Brigade soldiers near Kfar Tebnit. After the 1 June mutual cessation, a 19 June truce mediated by the US, Qatar and Iran, and the 26 June Israel-Lebanon framework, large-scale combat ended. Fighting moved underground: the IDF took and demolished the Ali al-Taher ridge complex (3-11 September) and cleared Mansouri (28 September). The Lebanese death toll since 2 March reached 4,387 by 11 October.
situation: As of October 2026 Israel holds a security zone of roughly 570-600 sq km up to its Yellow Line, about 12 km deep in places and anchored on Beaufort, with winterised positions and plans for a fallback 'Gray Line' on ridges. The IDF says it will stay 'for years' and keeps striking Hezbollah; about 10 Hezbollah fighters were killed trying to cross the line during one brigade's rotation. The LAF is deploying in Nabatieh and pilot zones and seizing arms caches but does not confront Hezbollah directly. Hezbollah says it will cooperate on a state 'monopoly of arms' but will not give up its arsenal while Israel occupies Lebanese land. More than one million people were displaced and Israel bars return to the zone.
technical: Israeli divisions engaged: 36th, 91st, 146th, 162nd and 98th (98th from 7 Apr 2026); five divisions at peak (Wikipedia: 2026 Lebanon war).

Israeli-declared Yellow Line (18 Apr 2026) encloses 55 towns and villages, including parts of Marjayoun District north of the Litani and the Shebaa area; occupied area about 570-600 sq km (Wikipedia).
Evacuation orders covered about 2,000 sq km south of the Zahrani River, plus Dahiyeh (Wikipedia: Israeli occupation of Southern Lebanon).
Operation Eternal Darkness, 8 Apr 2026: more than 100 targets in southern Lebanon, Beirut and the Bekaa in ten minutes; at least 357 killed (Wikipedia).
Bridges: Qasmiyeh bridge over the Litani destroyed 22 Mar; Dallafa bridge hit 23 Mar; last link south of the Litani cut 15-16 Apr (Wikipedia).
Hezbollah fired up to about 2,000 rockets and drones; UNIFIL tracked 210+ missiles by 5 Mar (Wikipedia).
Hezbollah ATGM use from 4 Mar; a Puma engineering vehicle and a D9 bulldozer hit on 8 Mar, two soldiers killed (Wikipedia).

Fibre-optic FPV drones from late Apr 2026, which radio-frequency jamming cannot stop; largest coordinated drone attack 12 May in three waves on one target; a drone near Kfar Tebnit killed four 401st Brigade soldiers including a lieutenant-colonel (Wikipedia; Timeline of the 2026 Lebanon war).

Ali al-Taher ridge: IDF says it destroyed more than 2 km of tunnels of the Badr Unit command complex; wider Ali al-Taher-Beaufort network had eight routes totalling 5.4 km; 1,100+ tonnes of explosives; USGS recorded a M4.1 event (LWJ, 11 Sep 2026).
Brigade clearing tallies: 55th Reserve Paratroopers destroyed 600+ Hezbollah sites and eight underground routes; Golani 900+ sites over seven months (LWJ, 7 Oct 2026).
Hezbollah tunnel at Majdal Zoun about 200 m long (LWJ, Jul 2026).

Senior Hezbollah losses: Makled (intel, 2 Mar), Radwan commander Abu Khalil Barji (c. 22-23 Mar), Southern Front commander Hajj Yusuf Ismail Hashem (1 Apr), Radwan senior commander Ahmed Ghaleb Balout (6 May) (Wikipedia).
UNIFIL: three Indonesian peacekeepers killed 29-30 Mar and two French soldiers killed (18 and 22 Apr) (Wikipedia).

June 26 framework: 14 points plus Security Annex; pilot zones (clear, third-party verify, LAF maintain, rebuild); 24/7 military coordination mechanism; Israeli withdrawal phased and conditions-based; US aid tied to milestones (LWJ, 13 Jul 2026).
LAF seizures in pilot zones: 1,818 weapons and ammunition items, about 86% light ammunition (LWJ, Sep 2026).
IDF death toll in Lebanon reached 37 by about early May 2026 (Timeline of the 2026 Lebanon war); a later total was not retrieved.
casualties: Lebanese Health Ministry: 4,387 killed and 12,424 wounded from 2 Mar to 11 Oct 2026; 8,954 killed since 8 Oct 2023 (LBCI, 11 Oct 2026). The ministry does not distinguish fighters from civilians; Israel claims large numbers of Hezbollah fighters among the dead (e.g. 100+ in Bint Jbeil alone). The toll rose only from 4,383 (10 Sep) to 4,387 (11 Oct) despite reported deadly strikes, so recent reporting may lag. Israeli losses: at least 37 soldiers killed in Lebanon by early May 2026, plus civilians in the north (Wikipedia timeline); overall Israeli war figures for the Iran war period are 40 soldiers and 31 civilians killed (Wikipedia: 2026 Iran war). Five UN peacekeepers killed (Wikipedia).
displaced: More than 1.2 million Lebanese displaced, over 20% of the population (Wikipedia: Israeli occupation of Southern Lebanon (2026)); Israel bars return to the security zone, and Katz said on 24 Jun 2026 that '200,000 residents will not return'.

timeline.event: Israel kills Hezbollah chief of staff Haytham Ali Tabatabai in Beirut (Nov 2025).
LAF says phase one of disarmament south of the Litani is complete.
US and Israel launch war on Iran; Khamenei killed.
Hezbollah fires on northern Israel; Israel strikes Beirut, Bekaa and the south; Lebanon bans Hezbollah military activity.
IDF begins ground operation to create a 'forward defense area'.
Katz announces demolition of border villages and control up to the Litani.
Operation Eternal Darkness: 100+ targets in ten minutes, at least 357 killed.
IDF says it has encircled Bint Jbeil.
IDF declares Yellow Line zone covering 55 towns and villages.
IDF Litani crossing raid ends; Hezbollah's largest drone attack of the war.
IDF captures Beaufort Castle, Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and Yohmor.
Israel-Hezbollah truce mediated by the US, Qatar and Iran.
Israel-Lebanon framework agreement signed; Hezbollah rejects it.
IDF demolishes Ali al-Taher ridge tunnel complex; withdraws to Beaufort next day.
Golani Brigade leaves southern Lebanon after seven months.
Health Ministry toll since 2 Mar reaches 4,387 killed.

outlook: Watch whether Israel formalises the fallback 'Gray Line', whether the LAF moves from seizing caches to dismantling Hezbollah infrastructure north of the Litani (the step Hezbollah warns could mean civil war), whether displaced residents are ever allowed back to the 55 villages, and whether the US-Iran track holds, since Hezbollah's restraint has tracked Tehran's. Renewed strikes on Dahiyeh would signal collapse of the 1 June understanding.

zones.note: Hezbollah command and Al-Manar hit Mar-May 2026; off-limits under 1 Jun understanding.

zones.note: Strikes on command centres and depots, including Feb 2026 and throughout the war.

battles.name: Battle for Ali al-Taher Ridge and demolition of the Badr Unit complex
battles.place: Ali al-Taher Ridge, southeast of Nabatieh, Lebanon
battles.outcome: IDF demolished the complex and withdrew to Beaufort, claiming fire control of the ridge; Hezbollah called it an organised withdrawal from a 'rear base'.
battles.forces: IDF 36th Division, Commando Brigade, Yahalom, Golani reconnaissance; more than 1,100 tonnes of explosives.
battles.losses: Several Hezbollah operatives killed per IDF footage; two IDF soldiers lightly wounded; 12 killed in the Israeli strike on nearby Kfar Rumman, including two children and a paramedic (Lebanese Health Ministry via LWJ).
battles.significance: Largest post-ceasefire operation; destroyed more than 2 km of tunnels in a 5.4 km network, illustrating that the June truce left Israel free to keep clearing Hezbollah infrastructure.

sources.label: FDD's Long War Journal: IDF destroys Hezbollah underground command complex at Ali al Taher (11 Sep 2026)

battles.name: Battle of Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and capture of Beaufort Castle
battles.place: Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, Yohmor and Beaufort Castle, Nabatieh Governorate, Lebanon
battles.outcome: Israeli victory; Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, Yohmor and nearby towns occupied and Beaufort Castle captured.
battles.forces: IDF 36th Division elements crossing the Litani and taking Beaufort Ridge 'from an unexpected direction' (LWJ).
battles.losses: Not given in retrieved sources; daily Lebanese tolls averaged over 50 on 27-28 May (Wikipedia).
battles.significance: Beaufort's crusader castle and ridge dominate the Litani bend and Nabatieh; it became the anchor of Israel's security zone and of the later Ali al-Taher operation.

battles.name: Battle of Haddatha
battles.outcome: Hezbollah victory; Israeli incursion repelled and forces withdrew.
battles.forces: IDF tanks and infantry including the 401st Armored Brigade; Hezbollah ATGM and ambush teams.
battles.losses: 401st Armored Brigade commander (colonel) severely wounded on 20 May (Wikipedia: 2026 Lebanon war).
battles.significance: Rare clear tactical setback for the IDF, showing Hezbollah could still defend terrain outside the destroyed border belt.

battles.name: Israeli crossing of the Litani River
battles.place: Litani River near Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and Deir Siryan, Lebanon
battles.outcome: Israeli victory; northwestern bank of the Litani and outskirts of Zawtar al-Sharqiyah occupied.
battles.forces: IDF raid force; described as a weeklong raid in mid-May.
battles.significance: First crossing of the Litani in this war, breaking the river line that the 2006 UNSC Resolution 1701 framework used as the southern limit for Hezbollah.

battles.name: Battle of Bint Jbeil (2026)
battles.outcome: Israeli victory; city encircled by 13 Apr and taken (end date approximate, before 12 May).
battles.forces: IDF 98th Division (deployed 7 Apr) with armour and engineers; Hezbollah urban defence.
battles.losses: IDF claimed more than 100 Hezbollah fighters killed in the city by 13 Apr; Al Jazeera imagery (28 Apr) showed about 90% of the urban area destroyed or badly damaged and 3,000 housing units levelled (Wikipedia).
battles.significance: Bint Jbeil is symbolic for Hezbollah (Nasrallah's 2000 'spider web' speech, 2006 battle); its near-total destruction illustrates Israel's buffer-zone method of clearing and razing border towns.

battles.name: Operation Eternal Darkness
battles.place: Southern Lebanon, Beirut and the Bekaa, Lebanon (plotted at Dahiyeh)
battles.outcome: Israel hit more than 100 targets in ten minutes, hours after the US-Iran ceasefire was announced, making clear Lebanon was excluded.
battles.forces: Israeli Air Force mass simultaneous strike package.
battles.significance: The single deadliest day of the 2026 Lebanon war; it decoupled the Lebanon front from the Iran ceasefire and pushed Washington into brokering a separate Lebanon truce on 16 April.

sources.label: Wikipedia: 2026 Lebanon war

battles.name: Strike on Nabi Chit, Bekaa
battles.outcome: Mass-casualty strike in a Hezbollah-heartland village.
battles.losses: More than 41 killed, including at least three Lebanese Army soldiers (Wikipedia: 2026 Lebanon war).
battles.significance: Early sign that the Lebanese Army, not a party to the war, would also take losses.

sources.label: Wikipedia: 2026 Lebanon war

battles.name: Battle of Khiam (2026)
battles.outcome: Israeli victory; town occupied and depopulated; former Khiam detention centre demolished (satellite imagery 23 Mar).
battles.forces: IDF ground forces entering from 3-4 Mar; heavy fighting 13-14 Mar; Hezbollah ATGM and IED defence.
battles.significance: Khiam anchors the eastern sector overlooking the Marjayoun plain and Israel's Galilee panhandle; its fall opened the route toward Beaufort and Shebaa.

battles.name: Opening Israeli air campaign on Beirut and Dahiyeh
battles.outcome: Hezbollah intelligence chief and Quds Force commanders killed; Al-Manar HQ and ten high-rises hit.
battles.forces: Israeli Air Force: strikes from 3am on 2 Mar, Al-Manar TV HQ (3 Mar), ten high-rises used as HQs (6 Mar), Ramada hotel (8 Mar), unannounced central Beirut strikes (18 Mar).
battles.losses: Intelligence chief Hussain Makled killed (IDF claim, 2 Mar); at least 10 killed and 27 injured on 18 Mar alone (Wikipedia: 2026 Lebanon war).
battles.significance: Israel went straight for Hezbollah's command and Iran's officers in Beirut, signalling a war aimed at dismantling the group rather than containing it.

sources.label: Wikipedia: 2026 Lebanon war

battles.name: Israeli strikes on Hezbollah command centres, Baalbek area
battles.outcome: Hezbollah command sites hit; Lebanese president condemned a 'new violation of Lebanon's sovereignty'.
battles.forces: Israeli air strikes; same day strike on Ein el-Hilweh camp near Sidon.
battles.losses: At least 10 killed and 24 wounded, including three children; Hezbollah said eight members were among the dead (Lebanese Health Ministry via AP).
battles.significance: Last major strikes before the war restarted, showing the pre-March truce was already eroding as the US weighed action on Iran.

sources.label: Hawaii Tribune-Herald (AP): Israeli strikes in Lebanon's Bekaa kill at least 10

battles.name: Strike killing Hezbollah chief of staff Haytham Ali Tabatabai, Beirut
battles.outcome: Hezbollah's top military commander killed; Hezbollah did not retaliate at the time.
battles.forces: Israeli Air Force precision strike on a building in Beirut's southern suburbs.
battles.losses: Tabatabai killed (Wikipedia: 2026 Lebanon war; AP via Hawaii Tribune-Herald); other casualties not given in retrieved sources.
battles.significance: Hezbollah later called the April 2026 death of its Southern Front commander its harshest loss since Tabatabai, showing how deeply the 2024-26 decapitation campaign had cut into its command.
